scenario: A happy, proud cartoon DOG wearing a collar with a round vaccination tag (paw-print + shield icon) sits for a gentle head-pat from a single friendly hand+sleeve (no full human figure). Beside the dog, a cheerful ROUND SHIELD character with a paw-print on its chest cheers 'hooray'. In the opposite corner a small friendly cartoon BAT waves hello from a clear distance, calm and harmless, not landing on the dog. Deliberately different scenario from the heartworm page in this same set (which uses a monthly-treat + calendar + mosquito scene) — this one is about the yearly rabies vaccine and shows a bat as a wildlife reservoir species depicted as approachable-but-distant, not something to touch.

prompt:
A black-and-white CHILDREN'S COLORING BOOK page, square 1:1, 1080x1080. Composition must be SQUARE, never wide or landscape.

CRITICAL — READ FIRST: (a) the drawing must BLEED OFF ALL FOUR EDGES with NO frame, NO border line, NO box and NO white margin band; (b) this is a ZOOMED-IN close-up composition — the dog, hand and shield character must run past every edge of the square, filling the whole frame; (c) NO decorative starburst, radiating burst, sparkle rays, sunbeam rays or any lines radiating outward from any character anywhere in the image.

SCENE: A big, happy, proud cartoon DOG stands in the middle of the picture, tail wagging (drawn mid-wag as a curved motion shape), tongue out, eyes closed in a contented smile. The dog wears a simple round collar with a single big VACCINATION TAG hanging from it — the tag is a plain circle with a small paw-print and a small rounded shield shape drawn inside it (no text, no letters). A single friendly, simple cartoon HAND with a bit of sleeve (no full human body or face) reaches in from one side to give the dog a gentle pat on the head. Beside the dog, a cheerful ROUND SHIELD character floats happily — a simple rounded shield outline with a big smiling face (two dot eyes, a wide closed-mouth smile) and a small paw-print on its chest, its two little cartoon arms raised in a joyful "hooray" pose. In the opposite corner, a small, round, friendly cartoon BAT character flies past at a clear distance, simple oval body, two big soft rounded wings, a small smiling face, one wing raised in a cheerful wave hello — calm, harmless, not landing on or approaching the dog. Everything large, simple, chunky and warm, with generous open white areas inside every shape so a child can colour them in.

STYLE — coloring book line art:
- BOLD, THICK, EVEN BLACK OUTLINES on pure WHITE. Every shape fully closed.
- ABSOLUTELY NO shading, NO grey tones, NO hatching, NO stippling, NO cross-hatching, NO gradients, NO colour fill, NO solid black areas anywhere (eyes may have a small solid pupil only).
- Simple, cheerful, chunky cartoon shapes with plenty of white space.

STRICTLY FORBIDDEN — the page is rejected if any of these appear:
- ANY decorative STARBURST, comic-style radiating burst, "pow"/impact star, sparkle burst, twinkle burst, sunbeam rays, radiating speed lines, motion rays or halo of rays behind, around or under any character. NO radiating lines of any kind anywhere, including around the vaccination tag or the shield character. They leave a big empty shape that cannot be removed afterwards.
- ANY rectangle, rounded rectangle, square box outline, picture frame, panel edge, comic panel, border line, outer margin line, ground-line box, or vignette. The drawing must NOT sit inside a box of any kind. Do NOT draw a thin black line anywhere near the edge of the image. There must be NO white margin between the artwork and the image edge — the dog, hand, shield character and bat are CUT OFF by the image edge itself where they extend past it.
- The artwork must BLEED OFF ALL FOUR EDGES of the square — parts of the dog, the hand/sleeve, the shield character or the bat run right off the top, bottom, left and right edges, with no white margin band and no enclosing outline.
- NO text, letters, numbers, words, captions, labels, signatures or watermarks anywhere.
- NO speech bubble, thought bubble or balloon of any kind (one is added separately afterwards).
- NO virus shape, no bullet shape, no syringe, no needle, no blood, no sick or sad or foaming or distressed animal, nothing gruesome or scary.
- NO full human figure, no human face or body — only a single friendly hand and sleeve reaching in from off-frame.
- Do NOT draw the bat chasing, biting or landing on the dog — it must be flying calmly past at a distance, waving hello, clearly friendly and harmless in this scene.


FINAL REMINDER, most important rule of all: do NOT place this drawing inside a framed box, a bordered square, or a picture-on-a-wall layout. Imagine the canvas as a window that is too small for the scene — the dog's ear, the hand's sleeve, the shield character's raised arm, and the bat's wingtip must all be visibly SLICED OFF by the top/left/right/bottom edges of the image, the same way a photo crops off part of a subject that is too close to the camera. If you can trace a rectangle of blank white space or a black outline running all the way around the picture near the edge, that is WRONG — erase it and redraw the scene bigger, closer, so it overflows the frame on all four sides.

SCALE UP EVEN MORE: every character must be drawn approximately 20% larger than a natural fit, so that the dog's ear or head, the hand's sleeve, the shield character's arm AND the bat's wingtip are each individually cut off by a DIFFERENT edge of the square (one character per edge: top, bottom, left, right) — not just the left edge. Push the whole scene so far into close-up that all four edges each slice through at least one character.
